entities.summary:
Ingenuinus was the second historically confirmed bishop of Sabiona or Säben, venerated as a saint.

Born in the early 6th century CE, Ingenuinus served as bishop from approximately 585 to 605 CE. During his tenure, he played a crucial role in maintaining religious stability within the region. He also oversaw the construction of several churches and monasteries, leaving behind a lasting legacy in the spiritual lives of those under his care.

Ingenuinus's significance extends beyond his local influence, as he was part of a larger movement to preserve Christian traditions amidst the turmoil of the Migration Period. His dedication to his faith and community helped shape the regional identity of Sabiona/Säben for centuries to come.

As a testament to his enduring impact, Ingenuinus has been recognized as a saint by various Christian denominations, ensuring his name remains associated with devotion and spiritual guidance.

Ingenuinus's historical significance can be summarized in three dimensions: regional influence during the Migration Period, his role in preserving Christian traditions, and his lasting legacy in the region's religious landscape.
